messages.content: Provide the current weather information for Yosemite National Park at Mariposa, CA, using the coordinates 37.8651 N, 119.5383 W, and tell me the temperature, wind speed, and precipitation? I would like the temperature in Fahrenheit.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather information for a specified location using the Open-Meteo API. If using state, then use short form like CA. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The API endpoint for fetching weather data, with a default value pointing to the Open-Meteo API service.

location.description: The geographical location for which to retrieve weather data, in the format of 'City, State (abbr)' or 'Location, State (abbr)', such as 'San Francisco, CA'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for temperature values.

But function signature expects location string. We could pass something like "Yosemite National Park". However we also have coords. Maybe include them via query parameters manually.

Open-Meteo forecast requires latitude & longitude params. So we might construct URL ourselves: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&current_weather=true&precipitation_hours=1 etc. Actually open-meteo supports precipitation probability? For precipitation amount you may request hourly precipitation. Let's just fetch current weather includes temperature, windspeed, winddirection, weathercode, time. Precipitation isn't part of current_weather. Might need separate parameter: e.g., ?hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_sum. Then parse latest hour.

But simpler: Use current_weather plus precipitation_probability? Not available. Could approximate zero if no rainfall.

Let's attempt to call function with custom URL including all needed fields. We'll set unit fahrenheit. Provide location placeholder. We'll ask for current weather only. But precipitation missing. Perhaps we can still provide precipitation from hourly sum last hour.

Maybe better to make two calls: one for current weather, another for hourly precipitation. But tool limited to single invocation per response? Possibly multiple calls allowed sequentially. I'll do first call for current weather. Then second call for precipitation. Or combine into one call retrieving both current and hourly precipitation. Let's craft URL:

"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&current_weather=true&timezone=America%2FLos_Angeles"

For precipitation, add "&hourly=precipitation".

Then after getting result, compute precipitation for most recent hour. That will require parsing JSON. In this environment, calling function returns raw JSON. We can't process further unless we write code. But we can instruct assistant to interpret output. Since it's an LLM, it can read returned JSON.

Thus let's call once with combined request. Provide location string anyway. Unit f.
